source_caption:
There is a brilliant, undeniable irony in David Fincher casting Justin Timberlake as Sean Parker. In the early 2000s, Timberlake was at the absolute peak of the traditional music industry with *NSYNC, making him one of the biggest artists directly impacted by the massive financial disruption of Napster. A decade later, he delivered a wildly charismatic, career-defining performance playing the exact tech pioneer who helped dismantle the very musical empire he had built.
⠀
The Social Network (2010), directed by David Fincher, starring Jesse Eisenberg, Andrew Garfield, Justin Timberlake. A brilliant but deeply insecure Harvard student builds a global social media empire, only to alienate his closest friends and face ruthless legal battles in his relentless pursuit of success.

source_details.title: The Social Network
source_details.synopsis: The Social Network is a 2010 American biographical drama film directed by David Fincher and written by Aaron Sorkin. Based on the 2009 book The Accidental Billionaires by Ben Mezrich, the film portrays the founding of the social networking website Facebook. It stars Jesse Eisenberg as Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg, with Andrew Garfield as co-founder Eduardo Saverin, Justin Timberlake as Sean Parker, Armie Hammer as Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, and Max Minghella as Divya Narendra. Neither Zuckerberg nor any other Facebook staff were involved with the project, although Saverin was a consultant for Mezrich's book. Production began when Sorkin signed on to write the screenplay.
